name: Biology: Spatial transcriptomic cell abundance inference
description: Infer nonnegative spatial cell counts from reference expression signatures and evaluate separate held-out genes using a count likelihood.

sources.locator: cell2location Methods: reference signatures, spatial count decomposition and constructed-mixture validation.
Official author implementation/data reference; evaluator and seed are independently written, not copied.

requirements.datasets: Pinned source-derived bundle B06.json plus SHA256 manifest under .cache/science-biology; prepare using scripts/prepare_biology_expansion.py. Requires matched measured spatial counts and reference signatures with absolute scale and independent gene blocks; selected upstream inferred-abundance outputs are not ground truth.

evaluation.benchmark: Biology: Spatial transcriptomic cell abundance inference
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: deconvolve(spatial_counts, reference_profiles, coordinates) -> nonnegative spots x cell_types absolute abundances. Inputs include training genes only and calibrated per-cell signatures. Minimize Poisson NLL of separate held-out genes, using trusted full reference profiles. Known constructed-mixture composition is diagnostic only.

provenance.note: New local evaluator and seed based on cited source specifications; official data are reused.

limitations: Fixed absolute-scale signatures and local Poisson likelihood are a reduced adaptation; full cell2location accounts for additional technical variation. Real-tissue abundance truth is not assumed.
Public source subsets are development-visible. Freeze candidates before evaluating on additional independently chosen studies/instances; trusted candidate execution is not a security sandbox.
Improving this benchmark is a scientific-method result; it does not alone establish a new biological discovery.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Infer the cellular composition of tissue locations from spatial transcriptomic counts.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Mapping cell types in tissue helps investigate tissue organization and interactions between cellular populations.

papers.title: Cell2location maps fine-grained cell types in spatial transcriptomics
papers.primary_goal: Resolve spatial locations and abundance of fine-grained cell types by combining reference single-cell signatures with spatial transcriptomics.
papers.task_relation: The local nonnegative cell-count deconvolution and held-out-gene likelihood preserve this inference target. They do not reproduce the full cell2location hierarchy or establish that inferred cell counts are experimentally correct.
